newsitem.title: USA: Chicago $32 mln deal set for July -- CFO.
newsitem.headline: Chicago $32 mln deal set for July -- CFO.

text.p: Chicago Chief Financial Officer Walter Knorr said Wednesday the city hopes to begin a negotiated sale later this month of about $32.5 million of building acquisition certificates to fund purchase and renovation of a now-vacant building for municipal use.
George K. Baum & Co has been selected as underwriter and Chapman & Cutler as bond counsel for the transaction, which could close in early August, Knorr said.

The city anticipates funding the projected $2.7 million annual debt service on the certificates by cutting its operational costs from about $4 million in the current antiquated building to approximately $1 million in the renovated facility, Knorr said.
It is the first time that the city has sought to issue certificates in this manner, Knorr said. The city expects to solicit for insurance on the issuance, which will cover 23 years, he added.

About $27 million of the proceeds would go to acquire and rehabilitate the building and an estimated $5 million to $5.5 million to cover anticipated debt service costs for the projected two years of construction, Knorr said.
The City Council approved the issuance of up to $35 million of certificates Wednesday to buy and renovate the building, a former Goldblatt's store northwest of downtown Chicago.

Once renovations are complete, the city plans to relocate as many as 500 workers from their current offices in the Kraft Building in a rapidly developing neighborhood just northeast of downtown near Lake Michigan.
Kraft Corp had ceded the building to Chicago for $1 in 1981, but the land underneath is owned by Chicago Dock and Canal Trust. The city lease on the property expires in 2017.
Once vacated, the city plans to offer the Kraft property for bid, with or without the building, Knorr said.
